text: Vuoi qualcosa di fresco da bere. Cosa chiedi? → You want something fresh to drink. What do you ask for?
why: 'Fresco' here means cool or cold, not fresh; the English points the learner at the wrong meaning.
fix: You want something cold to drink. What do you ask for?

text: Non sai dire una parola in italiano. Cosa chiedi? → You can't say a word in Italian. What do you ask?
why: In English 'You can't say a word in Italian' means you can't speak any Italian at all, not that one word is missing.
fix: There's a word you don't know how to say in Italian. What do you ask?

text: Quanto costano i biscotti? → How much are the biscuits?
why: To the American learner, 'biscuits' are a bread roll; biscotti here are cookies.

text: Un'aranciata, per favore. → An orangeade, please.
why: 'Orangeade' is rare in American English; an aranciata is an orange soda.

text: Abito qui, in via … → I live here, in … Street.
why: British usage; American English lives 'on' a street.

text: Abito in via … → I live in … Street.
why: British usage; American English lives 'on' a street.

text: Ha moneta? → Have you got any change?
why: British phrasing for an American learner.

text: Mi dispiace, non ho spiccioli. → Sorry, I haven't got any change.
why: British phrasing for an American learner.
fix: Sorry, I don't have any change.

text: Mi dispiace, non ho spiccioli. → Sorry, I haven't got any change.
why: British phrasing for an American learner.
fix: Sorry, I don't have any change.

text: È qui in vacanza? → Are you here on holiday?
why: 'On holiday' is British; an American says 'on vacation'.

text: Sei qui in vacanza? → Are you here on holiday?
why: 'On holiday' is British; an American says 'on vacation'.

text: È qui in vacanza? → Are you here on holiday?
why: 'On holiday' is British; an American says 'on vacation'.

text: Sei qui in vacanza? → Are you here on holiday?
why: 'On holiday' is British; an American says 'on vacation'.

text: Ed è qui in vacanza? → And are you here on holiday?
why: 'On holiday' is British; an American says 'on vacation'.
fix: And are you here on vacation?

text: Buonasera, signora. → Good evening, madam.
why: 'Madam' is far stiffer in English than everyday 'signora'.

text: Buonasera, signora! → Good evening, madam!
why: 'Madam' is far stiffer in English than everyday 'signora'.

text: Puoi ripetere? → Could you repeat that? (to a friend)
why: The parenthetical explains instead of translating; it belongs in a note, not the English line.

text: Sono americano. → I'm American. (a man says this)
why: The parenthetical explains instead of translating; it belongs in a note.

text: Sono americana. → I'm American. (a woman says this)
why: The parenthetical explains instead of translating; it belongs in a note.

text: Sono inglese. → I'm English. (a man or a woman)
why: The parenthetical explains instead of translating; it belongs in a note.

text: Di mattina, cosa chiedi da bere per voi due? → In the morning, what do you ask for to drink for the two of you?
why: Word-for-word and clumsy, with a doubled 'for'.
fix: It's morning. What do you order for the two of you to drink?

text: In quale paese abiti? → In which country do you live?
why: Stiff word order that follows the Italian.
fix: Which country do you live in?

text: Un amico ti dice: «Ciao, come stai?» Cosa rispondi? → A friend says to you: 'Hi, how are you?' What do you answer?
why: 'What do you answer?' and 'says to you:' copy the Italian; English says 'What do you say?'.
fix: A friend says, 'Hi, how are you?' What do you say?

text: Una signora anziana ti dice: «Come sta?» Cosa rispondi? → An older lady says to you: 'How are you?' What do you answer?
why: 'What do you answer?' and 'says to you:' copy the Italian; English says 'What do you say?'.
fix: An older lady says, 'How are you?' What do you say?

text: Un negoziante ti dice: «Come sta?» Cosa rispondi? → A shopkeeper says to you: 'How are you?' What do you answer?
why: 'What do you answer?' and 'says to you:' copy the Italian; English says 'What do you say?'.
fix: A shopkeeper says, 'How are you?' What do you say?

text: Il cassiere chiede: Ha moneta? Tu non hai spiccioli. Cosa rispondi? → The cashier asks if you have change. You have none. What do you answer?
why: 'What do you answer?' and 'says to you:' copy the Italian; English says 'What do you say?'.
fix: The cashier asks, 'Do you have any change?' You don't. What do you say?

text: Il tuo amico ordina un caffè. Tu prendi la stessa cosa. Cosa dici? → Your friend orders a coffee. You have the same. What do you say?
why: 'You have the same' is unclear in English; it means you want the same thing.
fix: Your friend orders a coffee. You want the same. What do you say?
